title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — first sense: immanent act in God's mind
pass_a_gloss: Pick the first, and imputation is God's own inward act: nowhere but in God, in God's mind. Some call mind-and-will acts 'toward the outside' because creatures are their object—yet they stay immanent. The learned man here makes them less so, rather inconsiderately.
pass_b_english: If you choose the first, it is an immanent action of God: for it is not elsewhere, nor can it be, than in God, in God's mind. Some theologians indeed call the actions of the divine mind and will actions toward the outside, because they have creatures for their object: but they do not therefore make them less immanent, as the learned man does in this place, rather inconsiderately.
source_text: Si primum eligis, actio est Dei immanens: non enim alibi est aut esse potest quam in Deo, in Dei mente. Vocant quidem nonnulli Theologi actiones divinae mentis & voluntatis, actiones ad extra, quia habent pro obiecto creaturas: at non eas ideo faciunt minus immanentes, ut facit hoc loco vir doctus, <PRIVATE_ADDRESS> inconsiderate.

choices.choice: Mind-judgment is immanent in God, not 'into' us
